title: Track mattes and adjustment layers
summary: Reveal a title through an animated track matte, then soften the picture with an adjustment layer.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
A track matte shows a layer only through the layer above it. Unlike a mask it can be soft, and it shows while you edit. An adjustment layer changes everything below it: blur, color, tint.

The Reveal layer holds a black bar that slides across the stage; under it is the Title.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. The black bar slides across the title.

steps.title: Use it as a matte
steps.text:
Press Enter again to stop. Right-click the Title layer's name and choose Track Matte > Alpha Matte.

The bar above is no longer drawn: the title shows only where the bar is.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. The title is wiped on as the bar slides in.

steps.title: Add a layer
steps.text: Press Enter again to stop. Click the Reveal layer's name, then click the New Layer button under the layers, or choose Insert > Timeline > Layer. The new layer goes above it, on top.

steps.title: Make it an adjustment layer
steps.text: Right-click the new layer's name and choose Adjustment Layer. Everything below it blurs, and the Behaviors panel shows its Blur effect.

steps.title: Set the blur
steps.text: Click an empty part of the stage so nothing is selected. Set Radius (pixels) to 2 for a soft glow, or key it from 20 down to 0 for a title that comes into focus.

steps.title: Color too
steps.text: Click Add Effect and choose Tint or Color Correction: a night look, a flashback, a faded picture. Draw a shape on the adjustment layer and the effects apply only under it.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You revealed a title through a track matte and changed the picture with an adjustment layer.

A Luma Matte uses the light of the layer above instead of its shape: a soft gradient makes a soft wipe.
